input.quote: 16.5 Disclaimer of Liability for Consequential Damages. UNLESS EXPRESSLY PROVIDED HEREUNDER, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY OR ANY OF ITS RESPECTIVE AFFILIATES AND THEIR RESPECTIVE OFFICERS, DIRECTORS AND EMPLOYEES BE LIABLE UNDER THIS AGREEMENT FOR SPECIAL, INDIRECT, PUNITIVE, INCIDENTAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES SUFFERED BY THE OTHER PARTY UNDER THIS AGREEMENT
input.rationale: Section 16.5 is the only limitation-of-liability provision in the Agreement: it is a mutual exclusion of special, indirect, punitive, incidental and consequential damages, with carve-outs preserving third-party indemnity payments under Article 10 and Sections 16.1/16.2 and disapplying the limitation for gross negligence or willful misconduct. However, a document-wide search ("aggregate liability", "shall not exceed", "liable", "limitation of liability") returns no monetary cap of any kind — the only "shall not exceed" language is milestone/royalty mechanics in Article VI. Both parties therefore bear unlimited direct liability, including Ono's broad product-liability and Article 15 breach exposure. That fails even the fallback, which requires a mutual cap (12 months' fees) with carve-outs; the exclusion of consequential damages and the existing carve-outs are helpful but are not a cap. The clause is mutual, so this is not walk-away territory (Ono is not capped while Array is uncapped), and we have kept the edit to a single appended sentence in 16.5 rather than restructuring Article 16: a mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' payments by Ono and USD 1,000,000, with indemnification, confidentiality/data protection, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement outside the cap (mirroring the existing 16.5 carve-outs) and Ono's payment obligations excluded from the cap basis.

ops.oldText: PROVIDED, FURTHER, THAT THE FOREGOING LIMITATION OF LIABILITY SHALL NOT APPLY IN THE CASE OF GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT.
ops.newText: PROVIDED, FURTHER, THAT THE FOREGOING LIMITATION OF LIABILITY SHALL NOT APPLY IN THE CASE OF GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT. EXCEPT FOR EXCLUDED CLAIMS, EACH PARTY'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED THE GREATER OF (A) THE AMOUNTS PAID OR PAYABLE BY ONO TO ARRAY UNDER THIS AGREEMENT IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM AND (B) USD 1,000,000. FOR PURPOSES OF THE FOREGOING, "EXCLUDED CLAIMS" MEANS A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY, DATA PROTECTION OR DATA SECURITY OBLIGATIONS, ITS INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS UNDER ARTICLE 10 AND SECTIONS 16.1 AND 16.2, ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE, WILLFUL MISCONDUCT OR FRAUD, AND ITS INFRINGEMENT OF THE OTHER PARTY'S INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS; AND ONO'S OBLIGATION TO PAY AMOUNTS PROPERLY DUE UNDER THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT CONSTITUTE DAMAGES SUBJECT TO SUCH CAP.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 16.5 excludes consequential damages but leaves both parties' direct liability entirely uncapped, so we have added a mutual aggregate cap at the greater of twelve months' payments and USD 1,000,000, consistent with our position. Indemnification, confidentiality/data protection, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit outside the cap, and Ono's payment obligations are not treated as capped damages.
proposal.summary: Add a mutual aggregate liability cap with standard uncapped carve-outs to Section 16.5.
